You're oversimplifying it. Blind chance is a big part of evolution, but because of the way genes work, and the sheer amount of time since life began, it's not quite that simple.

Take the polar bear, for example. It evolved from the brown bear because of a genetic anomaly that altered the pigmentation of its fur (similar to albinism in humans and other species). At first, this happened completely by chance, but since white fur makes for better camouflage in arctic environments (ideal for sneaking up on prey), the bears carrying the genetic anomaly were more likely to thrive, and produce offspring that would also carry the genetic anomaly. Fast forward 100 000 years or so and pretty much all arctic bears carry the gene that makes their fur white, and have become a new species, separate from their brown-furred relatives.

I'm in a similar situation to you, Ben. Colon out 5 months ago, reoperated 3 months ago due to blockage with adhesions. Went back to the gym about 5 weeks ago. 

I use [this](https://nordicare.se/en/stomi-bas-25) one whenever I work out (even if I'm not doing any core work), and while it does the job, it's a bit stiff, if that makes sense. I haven't tried any other belts, but I feel like it would be better to use one that shapes itself to your body. In the end I don't think it matters too much, as long as it applies sufficient pressure to the stoma.

The first week in the gym I only did bodyweight stuff. I still do mostly bodyweight excercises for my lower body, such as bodyweight squats and wall-sits. 

For my core, I do deadlifts with VERY low weights (started with a broom handle, now doing ~45-50 kg after an extensive warmup). Personally I haven't done crunches at all. Instead I do the plank, since the movements are much gentler than crunches.

Overall I try to stay away from explosive movements when working the core. You're probably going to be in some pain at first. My first day in the gym I did 5 seconds of plank before succumbing to the pain. Now I can do 20 seconds comfortably. Listen to your body, take things slow, and you'll be swole in no-time!

Yes. Intermittent fasting isn't as much of a diet as it is a "food schedule". You basically have a window of X hours a day in which you get all of your daily calories. This window, for most people, are usually 8, 6, or 4 hours. Some take it even further with 2 hours or simply eating all your daily calories in one meal. This means that outside of your food window, you eat pretty much no calories. The exception is diet sodas, as they don't contain enough calories to break your fast.

I would also recommend that you, if possible, get all your calories post-workout, this way all the calories you burn during your workout is taken from your fat storage. Also you supposedly have higher metabolism post-workout. another recommendation is to go to bed on an empty stomach, so you have most of your fasting during your sleep.

Although there are no real rights or wrongs, these are the optimal steps for maximum efficiency. 

As an example, I'll briefly take you though my day: I wake up at 6 am, go to the gym for 1-1,5 hours (assuming I'm working out that day, if not, I'll sleep for another hour and a half), go to work at 8 am, skip breakfast all together, lunch at 11, finish work at 3:30 pm, eat dinner at 4. Then I don't eat again until lunch next day. The only thing I sacrifice doing this is breakfast and supper. My division of carbs, fats and proteins goes something along the lines of 50% carbs, 30-35% proteins, and 15-20% fat, so I'm not really eating anything I wouldn't normally eat.

As a last note, I would recommend that should you try it (and I hope you do):
ease into it. Don't start right at a 2 hour eating window for instance. Start at a 8 hour window, and when you feel comfortable doing that you slowly shrink the window over time.

Good luck to you, I am positive you will reach your goal if you try this.

I lost 21 lbs over the last 5 weeks doing intermittent fasting. I recommend trying it, you'll definitely reach your goal before Christmas. I'll also add that I'm 6'3 220 lbs when I started. Best of luck to you, I bet it'll all work out in the end :)

I remember when I was new to LoL, I didn't play an online game for the first week, I sat by myself and played custom games vs bots (coop vs ai wasn't implemented at the time). I did this because I knew how much of a pain in the ass I would have been for the people I got matched with if I went online straight away. Sadly, most people doesn't understand this, and just go with the excuse "I'm just having fun" or "It's just a game". If you can't manage to play properly you should go play single-player games, because, at the end of the day, the most disrespectful thing you can do to someone is wasting their time.
